sentences.text: Okay, Perfect.
Perfect.
I thought it was actually Ahmed joining and I was gonna say perfect timing.
I haven't.
You haven't.
It's just, it's just me and you.
It's okay otherwise.
All good, man?
Yeah, yeah.
No.
Great.

So I've been in digital marketing space for about eight years now and I've helped plethora of marketing agencies build their internal systems of operations to balance both internal growth and external growth.
Building business, strong business development department, well diversified to drive interest and build a consistent deal flow, pipeline of deal flow and continue to close deals.
But balance that with an internal systems to find the right talent, hire the right talent, train them in development over time.
And that's what organic growth look like, right?
Organic growth is painful.
Every time you pour more oil, you need to pour more oil on the other tube as well so you can balance it out.
And it's hard, right?
It takes a lot of time.
Most of the time companies will, if they forecast their growth to be organic, they will only add about 5 to 10, maximum 15%.
If they have good product market fit and a first mover advantage type of play, they will have a 20, 30, 40 easily.
But then M and A is the only route to go if you want to accelerate that growth and put it on steroids.
So yeah, my background is in engineering.
I love problem solving, I love building systems of operations and that's how I got into the digital marketing spaces through the operations, the operations side of the business.
In 2021 I co founded the marketing agency called the Greenhouse in the retention space.
I'm not sure how familiar are you with marketing.
So retention, think anything CRM, email marketing, SMS marketing, subscription loyalty programs, mail in mail as well services.
We've experienced tremendous growth over the last four years.
We scaled the company, we have about 16 full time employees all across the US now, all remote.

And as we continue to grow the Greenhouse, we're looking, we see the potential of what the Greenhouse could become when it's paired with four to six other agencies who are the best of the best in their service offerings.
So we're not only looking to diversify our service offerings and expand into different segments of marketing, but also we're looking to expand into different industries.

We currently have been working in the e commerce space and the healthcare and telehealth and tech space and we're looking to expand into other services like B2B, professional services and so on and so forth.
The ideal agency profile that could complement what we already have is an agency that provides both marketing services, paid Advertising with design and development.
The reason why is that we're looking for an agency to be the cornerstone of what the Greenhouse offers already.
Which will make it as well.
Yes.
An easier integration, but also make it a seamless bundle of services and complementary services.

When we're looking to add what we already offer in the retention space into web design and development or into acquisition on the paid ad side, those are the ideal targets for us to complete our first two deals.
Other than that, we're looking to build a 20 to $50 million marketing agency within next four years.
Our long term vision is to sell the acquired portfolio either to private equity or larger marketing company in the five year mark.
In the five year mark.
Okay, cool.
Very ambitious approach.
So I like that.
And the capital, is it a fund?
Have you raised a fund or is this just off the back of the investment from the Greenhouse?
Yes, it will be about an investment of the Greenhouse, self funded.
Plus we're looking into commercial or SBA debt.
Okay.
Getting debt.
Okay.
And you've got, I should imagine then you've got a small war fund that you're able to, you know, a war chest to put towards it.
Or is it all going to be SBA backed?
I only ask because some sellers are more interested in being acquired by a larger agency and stipulate they don't want to be acquired acquired by SBA backed loans.
But Reptile in particular are actually the other way.
They like the idea of being acquired by an SBA lender backed business.
Yeah, I mean we're open to all options.
I think that, I think our go to right now the go to option is obviously commercial lending or sba.
So whatever makes sense for us and for the seller, we're open to it.
Okay, cool.
All right, cool.
So I think you've signed a couple of NDAs on the site.
You want to give me an update on those assets or.
Let me just pull up file.
I don't think there'll be any particular updates to be honest with you.
Just was interested in what they were.
So it was project Reptile and there was definitely one other.
Which one?
Let me see.
I have here.
Last two I submitted yesterday, June 16th were the LA based Full Service D2C Marketing Agency and then a digital marketing agency with strong e commerce and web development foundation.
I submitted those yesterday.
Yeah, so the la, the la Direct consumer one, we've sold that and actually it's our fault because.
What agency was that was the name.
I can't, I can't disclose because the pricing obviously is on is on the site, so.
But the, the site wasn't working properly.
You were able to sign the NDA even though it was closed listed.
So that was my bad and that's.
Been fixed, no worries at all.
But yeah, so it's Project Reptile, isn't it?
That was the other one.
So.
So yeah, we can move things along and get you set up with the founders for a call.
So are you in the the country for the next week or so?
You're not going anywhere?
No.
Yeah, no.
Why is that?
Sorry, but why is that in the country?
Yeah, just to make sure you're, you're available over the next week or so.
Yeah, yeah, yeah, no, I'm pretty available.
You mean for a call with the founders of Lounge Lizard?
Yes, that's the one.
Yeah.
Cool.
Yeah.
What other information can you give me on Lounge Lizard, Andrew?
The reason, the reason for the sale.
So there's two founders involved, husband and wife.
The wife wants to step back and not be involved in the day to day running.
She does all the financials and managing the staff, that sort of thing.
The husband is a bit more flexible.

He would like to be either acquired by a large agency and stay in long time, full time for a long time, or he's happy for an SBA lender funded buyer to buy the business and him stay in for a short period of time under the assumption that an SBA loan operator would, would want him to leave the business so that they could run.
Could you repeat that again?
Yeah, so.
So, so most, not all.
Obviously in your situation this is, is different.
But a lot of buyers, when they're backed by an SBA loan, they are keen to operate the business themselves.
The, the SBA loan conditions used to be, but they've become more flexible.
Used to be that you had to buy with most of the cash up front and the founder needed to step out of the business.
Yeah, yeah, that's, that's completely different.
Completely the opposite of what we're trying to build.
Our dream outcome, our ideal bot seller profile is someone who wants the second bite of the apple.
Someone who sees the opportunity of what they've built and they want to grow it within a portfolio.
Obviously we're, we're agency founders too, so we already have the Greenhouse operator and we want to add to what the Greenhouse already offers.
So an ideal, an ideal seller profile would be someone who's willing to roll.
Over.
A good amount of equity.
When you take a good amount, what does that generally?
50, 50, 50, 50, 51, 49, 60, 40 split with some, you know, component of cash up front.
50 cash up front or 60 cash up front, they roll over the other 40.
And so we sell the portfolio in 5, 4 to 5 years.
Okay, all right, that's interesting.
Yeah, I think in this instance it's unlikely that they would want to do that.
But I will double, double check with them.
Okay.
What do you think they want?
What is it that they want?
So usually our sellers, they want, if they're going to roll over equity, it usually is a sort of minority shareholder.
Usually it's around 20, 30%.
With private equity it tends to be around 20, 30%.
But obviously all sorts of deals exist out there.
But that tends to be the general thing.
And so they are kind of more focused on the cash up front.
They want the majority of the cash up front.
And then usually there's some kind of earn out component over the next two or three years.
It can be shorter than that.
But we're very familiar with the sort of private equity approach where there is an equity rollover and then everybody exits together.
Obviously when it's a founder who is doing this for the first time, there's a lot of skepticism from the sellers.

So that's the kind of the key part that we need to overcome and make sure that our seller can really understand that, you know, you've got a track record, you run an agency yourself and that you've got, you know, like Dan back.
These are the sorts of things that we need to make sure that they understand.
But they still tend to not want a situation where their majority stake equity or a large part of the equity is rolled over.
So I'm just kind of being as transparent as possible.
But that's usually the mindset.
But I'll double check with these guys.
I'm sure they'll be happy to meet with you and discuss and then obviously down to you to give them the big pitch.
Yeah, absolutely.
I'm happy to do that just because I get it.
I understand that I've been pitching.

We have a few targets on the pipeline right now that we're talking to of market and I understand the challenge that most agency founders or even sellers will go through when they meet someone who is trying to do it for the first time, obviously.
But that's the reason why we have, we have, we have a board.
I've built a reputable dream team of people who have done it in the past, who have done mergers and acquisitions in the past and who have done it on a higher scale.
We have the, we've been Founders.

We've been in the transition of the agency game and just never wanted to be that agency founder who has been in the game building the same agency for 20 plus years, trying to grow it organically and then sticking, you know, get stuck on the threshold of the 3 and 4 million.
Why not build an agency and reach your TAM in the 2 million which closely where we are right now with the greenhouse and then scale it exponentially through M and A and that's how we envision it.
I totally agree with you Manir and actually I'm 100% backing founders like yourself.
I don't know if you see any of my content online but I talk a lot about roll ups and what you're doing.
The tricky part for the seller is they have to 100% agree or buy into your vision.
Even if they sold you a minority state, they are then locked in usually with the rest of the equity because it's not a liquid asset.
It is, you know, they can only sort of sell it once.
Even if they sold you 40% to get rid of the other 60% would be impossible.
They have to know that you can exit the entire deal because otherwise they're only getting less in terms of the price for their business.
They're only getting 40%.

So that's why most sellers want to sell 100% or something as close as possible to that because there's a massive trust issue in there and they're locked, their equity is locked to yours until you exit.
Fair enough.
It is a big deal but yeah look, you look like a good guy.
You dress smarter than me for this meeting as well, which usually a good sign.
So my recommendation will be to meet you in and go through what it is that they've got and see if it's a good fit for you.
Rock and roll.
Let's do that.
Would you?
Yeah, I'll just wait.
I'll get a follow up from you.
I'll wait until you just drop me some times and I'll confirm the availability for next week.
Yeah.
So next steps would be Ahmed chasing them up for some availability and then he'll be in touch with you for your availability as well.
Perfect.
Sounds great man.
Thank you Andrew, I appreciate it.
Yeah, no worries.
Good to meet you Manir.
Have a great day.
Thank you man.
You as well.
Cheers.
Take care now.

summary.overview:
- Mounir, co-founder of The Greenhouse, has 8 years in digital marketing and aims to build a $20-50 million agency in 4 years through M&A, targeting the retention marketing space.  
- The acquisition strategy focuses on obtaining 4-6 best-in-class marketing agencies to diversify services and complement existing retention offerings.  
- Funding will be a mix of self-funded investment from The Greenhouse and flexible commercial or SBA debt options, catering to seller preferences.  
- Currently signed NDAs involve a D2C marketing agency, an agency sold pre-NDA, and an active opportunity with Lounge Lizard, alongside other off-market targets.  
- Lounge Lizard's founders are considering options; the wife is looking to step back, while the husband is open to both long-term acquisition and short-term SBA transitions.  
- Mounir's ideal seller wants growth through portfolio expansion, preferring a deal structure with 50-60% cash upfront and equity rollover, while most sellers favor majority cash.  
- Establishing a reputable advisory board with M&A experience is a priority for Mounir to facilitate the intended aggressive scaling through acquisitions.  
- The goal is to exit the portfolio within 4-5 years, contingent on fostering trust with first-time acquirers due to equity illiquidity concerns.  
- The focus on expansion spans e-commerce, healthcare, and tech sectors, with a current interest in B2B and professional services.

summary.short_summary: Mounir, co-founder of The Greenhouse, seeks to establish a $20-50 million marketing agency within four years by acquiring 4-6 top-tier agencies in the retention marketing sector. The funding strategy involves a blend of self-investment and flexible debt options, tailored to sellers' preferences. Currently, NDAs are signed with various agencies, including Lounge Lizard, whose founders are contemplating acquisition options. Mounir's ideal seller is focused on portfolio growth, favoring a cash and equity rollover deal structure. He prioritizes forming a reputable advisory board with M&A expertise to support aggressive scaling efforts, aiming for an exit within 4-5 years while building trust with first-time acquirers. Expansion efforts will target e-commerce, healthcare, and tech sectors, with interests in B2B and professional services.
